drafted_from: tool:add-tool-source's own row (its words, input schema and sample run); read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Add a source of tools from this address" and give it the address, a folder's path, a git repository's https address or a remote MCP server's https address. It runs tool:add-tool-source and answers {"source":{"label":...,"kind":...,"learned":...},"entry":...,"approve":...,"said":...}. Nothing is added until you make the approve call yourself.
no_lists_because: It keeps one pending request per address (record:tool-source-request) until you approve or decline it; the sources you have are the engine's own list, read with tools:sources.
instructions: 1. Give your AI the address. A path starts with / or ~/. A git repository on GitHub, GitLab or Codeberg is its https address. A remote MCP server is its https address, written mcp+https://... when it is not plain; one of your own at a private address is mcp+http://host:port/path.

2. If the server asks you to sign in, the answer carries a sign_in address: open it, sign in on the server's own page, and the sign-in tool's page brings you back. The token is kept in your vault and your engine refreshes it; no AI sees it.
3. Read what comes back: kind says what the address is, learned says whether its syntax or one look at it told, and said says what happens next.

4. To add it, make the approve call yourself at your engine's door (tools:add-source at @tools with the input it gave). It starts with an empty grant: none of its tools may use your records, credentials or hosts until you say so.

worked_examples.title: A folder of your own tools
worked_examples.ask: Add a source of tools from /opt/example-tools/my-tools
worked_examples.hands_back: It answered {"source":{"label":"my-tools","kind":"folder","learned":"syntax"}} with the entry and the tools:add-source call for you to make; it asked the web nothing.
